notes.title: Meet the Indigenous Artists and Collaborators Behind Two Falls
notes.content:
We've recently received some comments asking who are the Indigenous artists and community members that contributed to the project. So here’s an introduction to the fantastic people who took part in the creation of Two Falls:

[h2]Isabelle Picard - Writer[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41514951/cae117b0e24e43cb18c2b7093238fcfb50f79763.png[/img]
Isabelle Picard is a Wendat ethnologist, speaker, columnist, host, and writer from Wendake. Among her many achievements, she wrote the first cultural policy for Wendake. Isabelle is behind the original story of Two Falls and is the creative force behind both Jeanne and Maikan. She crafted these two characters and the adventures they embark on throughout the game!
[url=https://x.com/IsabellePicard7]Follow Isabelle[/url]

[h2]Tara Miller - Art Director[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41514951/baf79a02f8c8ba74447beff072b430c33d6f61be.png[/img]
Tara Miller is a multidisciplinary Maliseet artist. She joined the project early on and dedicated herself to creating two distinct artistic worlds for each character. She is behind the creation of many key elements in the game.
[url=https://www.instagram.com/seaohso/]Follow Tara[/url]
[url=https://www.artstation.com/taramiller]Artstation[/url]

[h2]Anne-Marie "Éadsé" Gros Louis - Singer and Composer[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41514951/527da3dd1b67809d9a6d3203630e164c97dd1a53.jpg[/img]
Eadsé, meaning "My Good Friend" in Huron-Wendat, is a singer-songwriter from the Wendat Nation, based in Montreal. While she mainly explores pop and soul sounds, she skillfully adapted to Two Falls, creating a unique atmosphere by blending Indigenous instruments with more classical ones.
[url=https://www.instagram.com/eadsemusic/?hl=fr-ca]Follow Éadsé[/url]

[h2]Awastoki - 3D Artists[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41514951/20a38c90c581920c15ffde4946a6c303a070432b.png[/img]
“Awast Oki” is the Huron-Wendat name of Alexis, co-founder of the company, meaning “Beautiful Spirit.” Awastoki is a 3D creation company specializing in video games, board games, and industrial machinery. They immediately connected with Two Falls and were responsible for creating all the 3D elements and characters in the game.
[url=https://awastoki.com/]Discover Awastoki[/url]

[h2]Voice Actors[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41514951/6951b7fbae319b70267c644bd8bc2024ff2d7e00.png[/img]
[b]Charles Bender: [/b]A Wendat actor, host, translator, and director, deeply involved in sharing Indigenous culture. He voices Maikan in both English and French.
[b]James Malloch:[/b] A Mohawk actor and singer, he voices Tehonwastasta in English.

[h2]The Elders Council[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41514951/e712596c6674986acd3f6a6d2667bcf9ac7f390b.png[/img]
[b]Nionwentsïo Office:[/b] Their mission is to protect the fundamental rights of the Huron-Wendat Nation. They were particularly involved towards the end of the project, offering feedback on the game. They reviewed the texts, speech styles, reactions, actions, and visual elements, advising us on what needed to be changed, added, or removed.
[url=https://wendake.ca/cnhw/nionwentsio/]Discover Nionwentsïo Office[/url]
[b]Tshakapesh Institute:[/b] Their mission is to safeguard, transmit, preserve, and promote the Innu language and culture. They have been with us since the beginning. We met with people of all ages from their community, who shared legends and insights on topics such as hunting, respect for animals and nature, and their customs and realities. They also played a key role in guiding the direction of the game’s ending. They provided consultation and content validation throughout the project.
[url=https://www.tshakapesh.ca/]Discover Tshakapesh Institute[/url]

We hope you enjoyed meeting our partners! If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact us at stories@unreliablenarrators.games.

notes.title: Get to know our studio better
notes.content:
[b]For the love of games[/b]

First off, let’s get something out of the way: we LOVE video games. More specifically, we love narrative video games. And, from classics like Life is Strange and Detroit: Become Human to indie darlings such as What Remains of Edith Finch and Undertale, we’ve played them all.

After bingeing most of what was available, however, we realised that there aren’t that many story-driven games out there, especially when compared to other genres like shooters and platformers. Moreover, narrative games, or any video games for that matter, rarely feature characters from some groups, for instance indigenous or LGBTQ+ communities. At Unreliable Narrators, we believe these stories need to be told.



[b]There is no truth, only stories...[/b]

Humans tell stories. It’s in our nature. Stories we invent, stories we heard from friends, stories that go back generations. But as they are told and retold, they morph and evolve to become something different. In time, narrators inject their own perspectives so much that even historical events become… well, unreliable.

Our team wants to embrace these ambiguities to tell nuanced and rich tales, featuring characters that are generally misrepresented in the history books.



[b]Telling the “other side”[/b]

Take our first game, for example. Two Falls (Nishu Takuatshina) allows you to live the story through two unique perspectives.

There’s Jeanne, the young French woman, entrenched in her religious beliefs, and facing all the unknowns of this “New World”. After the wreckage of the boat on which she crossed the Atlantic, she is left alone with Capitaine, her loyal dog, to fend for her survival. To her, the land is menacing and frightening.

On the other side, Maikan, a young Innu, is trying to grasp the rapid changes his land is facing. To Maikan, nature is home, full of colors and wonders, but the way European settlers treat the land his ancestors have inhabited for thousands of years fills him with horror, as he witnesses the consequences of their actions.


[b]Stories that will make you think[/b]

As with Jeanne and Maikan, we want all the characters of our future games to be confronted in their beliefs. They will try to overcome the challenges they face by drawing on their own experiences, learning along the way that reality is often more complex than it seems at first glance.


We want our players to go through the same process as they play our games. Thanks to elaborate plotlines, human-like interactions, mature themes, and sometimes uncomfortable subject matters, we hope to help them see the world through a new lens.



[b]... and these are true stories.[/b]

To achieve this goal, we need our characters to be as authentic as possible. For example, Maikan can’t simply be our team’s conception of what an Innu is; he needs to talk and act like one. He needs to be an Innu.

Therefore, we are working very closely with Innu institutions, like the Tshakapesh Institute, and their elders to help validate our script, our scenes, and how our characters react to different situations, to make sure we are representing the Innu culture in the best way we can.

That is the process we want to go through for all our future games. Whether we tell the story of a forgotten Canadian Regiment that helped win World War I, or the brave people that fought for the Haïtian Revolution, we will always work in collaboration with experts and knowledge holders from the respective communities to help give a genuine voice to those who have been silenced for too long.

[i][b]Thank you![/b][/i]

We know we’ve said it quite a bit, but we’ll never be grateful enough for all the help your support provides. By contributing today to this [url=https://www.patreon.com/unreliablenarratorsgames]Patreon[/url], you not only allow us to create games that we all love immensely, you also help give a chance to other creators to tell their own stories.

[i]The Unreliable Narrators team.[/i]
